title: Can catering companies in Dubai set up a grazing table on-site?
body_markdown:
Yes. Catering companies in Dubai can assemble grazing tables at your venue, but you need to book on-site setup explicitly rather than assume it comes with delivery. For grazing table setup on site in Dubai, confirm who supplies the table, arranges the food, manages replenishment and clears away; these are separate responsibilities that your proposal should identify.


**TL;DR**

- Grazing table setup on site in Dubai needs an agreed setup scope, not just a food delivery booking.
- On-site assembly suits a styled display; delivered platters suit hosts comfortable arranging food themselves.
- myCHEF handles catering enquiries for households and businesses; confirm the grazing-table scope before booking.
- Ask separately about table hire, dietary handling, replenishment, serving staff and clearance.


## Can catering companies in Dubai set up a grazing table on-site?

Yes. The important distinction is between delivering food and building the display where your guests will eat. Your booking should state which service you are receiving, what equipment accompanies it and when the team finishes its responsibilities.

The guide to [grazing table catering companies in Dubai](https://www.mychef.ae/blog/best-grazing-table-catering-companies-in-dubai) is a related starting point when considering suppliers. For an on-site setup enquiry, use this sequence to make proposals easier to compare:

1. **Describe the occasion.** Explain whether the grazing table is a welcome spread, the main food offering or an accompaniment to another meal.
2. **Share the setting.** Send the venue address, photographs of the proposed position and any access instructions.
3. **Agree the menu.** Confirm guest numbers, dietary requirements and the balance of savoury food, bread, fruit and sweet items.
4. **Define the setup.** Identify who supplies the furniture, serving equipment, protective coverings and decorative elements.
5. **Set the handover.** Agree when the display must be ready and whether anyone remains to maintain it.
6. **Confirm the finish.** Record who clears food, collects equipment and handles waste.

**Book the setup you need, not just the food you want.** A photograph of a finished display does not establish what a supplier includes in your booking.

## What is the difference between on-site setup and platter delivery?

On-site assembly gives the caterer responsibility for arranging the agreed display at the venue. Platter delivery gives you prepared food to position yourself, unless additional setup is expressly included. Neither format automatically includes a member of staff staying throughout the event.

| Format | Best for | Main advantage | Main limitation |
|---|---|---|---|
| Delivered platters | Hosts happy to arrange the food | You control placement and presentation | You take responsibility for the final arrangement and guest-facing upkeep |
| On-site assembly | Hosts wanting the display arranged at the venue | The layout can be fitted to the agreed table and space | Access and setup time must be coordinated; ongoing service needs separate confirmation |
| Staffed grazing service | Events needing someone to maintain the spread | An agreed team can manage serving and replenishment tasks | Staffing duties and the service finish time need a clear written scope |

**Choose on-site assembly when presentation matters but you do not need continuous service.** Choose staffed service when you want someone responsible for the display after guests arrive.

Do not use “full setup” as a substitute for a task list. One proposal might mean arranging food on your dining table; another might include hired furniture and later collection. Compare the responsibilities, not the package label.

## What should an on-site grazing table proposal include?

A useful proposal separates food, presentation, equipment and labour. This prevents a common planning mismatch: expecting an event-ready display when the booking covers only prepared food and a brief handover.

Ask for written confirmation of the following:

- **Food scope:** the agreed menu, guest count and whether the spread supplements another meal.
- **Presentation scope:** platters, boards, risers, serving utensils and food labels.
- **Furniture scope:** whether the venue, host or caterer supplies the table and linen.
- **Setup scope:** delivery, unloading, assembly and the agreed ready time.
- **Service scope:** whether anyone remains, what they do and when they leave.
- **Clearance scope:** food removal, equipment collection, waste handling and any cleaning included.

Decorative flowers, candles and other styling should also have a named owner. Ask the caterer to approve anything positioned near the food rather than adding decorations after the display is finished.

Before paying a deposit, read the exclusions alongside the inclusions. A short exclusion such as “table not supplied” can change the practical work you need to organise.

## How should you prepare the venue?

Start with the table location, not the menu photograph. The caterer needs to understand the surface, access route and conditions before deciding how to arrange and manage the food.

### Confirm the table and surrounding space

Send photographs showing the whole area, not just a close-up of the tabletop. Include the route guests will use and any nearby doors, seating or other food stations.

Measure the usable surface and tell the caterer what it is made from. Ask what protection is needed underneath the display, whether hired equipment is suitable for that surface and how guests will reach the food without obstructing a doorway.

### Explain delivery and building access

For a Dubai apartment, villa or office, share the actual unloading route. Ask the venue or building management about delivery access, lift use, parking arrangements and any permissions they require.

Give the caterer a named contact who can admit the team. Do not assume reception staff, security or a concierge will know where the display belongs.

### Agree food holding and the handover

Ask how food will be held before service, what refrigeration or other facilities are needed and who follows the caterer’s handling instructions after handover. Setup completion and guest arrival are different milestones.

For an outdoor location, ask the caterer to assess the position, conditions and menu suitability. A shaded table alone is not a complete food-handling plan; agree an indoor alternative and the circumstances for using it.

## How does the setup process work on the day?

Agree a simple sequence before the event so the host, venue and catering team work towards the same handover. The following is a planning sequence, not a promised service timetable.

1. **Venue access:** the nominated contact admits the team and shows them the agreed position.
2. **Table preparation:** the responsible party checks the surface, protection and serving equipment.
3. **Food arrangement:** the team assembles the agreed display and identifies dietary items.
4. **Host handover:** the caterer explains serving arrangements, food handling and any remaining responsibilities.
5. **Clearance:** the agreed person or team removes food, clears equipment and manages collection.


![Five stages of on-site grazing table setup, from venue access to clearance](https://gwvckixiegkllthleuyt.supabase.co/storage/v1/object/public/workspace-article-images-public/a4cef1ee-9921-46b2-a45c-d05ccfc68e97/body-ba8f544104634cf961f67694e0c9c166.jpg)

*Agree who owns each stage before the catering team arrives.*


Keep the setup area accessible until handover. If other suppliers are dressing the same table or moving furniture, nominate someone to coordinate the work rather than leaving each team to resolve it on arrival.

## Why does the scope of a grazing table setup vary?

The work changes with the event, not simply the number of guests. Ask suppliers to explain how these factors affect the proposed service so you can compare like with like.

- **The role of the food:** a welcome spread and the main meal need different menu and portion discussions.
- **Menu complexity:** the selected food determines preparation, serving equipment and handling arrangements.
- **Venue access:** unloading distance, lifts and restricted access affect the setup plan.
- **Display requirements:** furniture, linen, boards, risers and decorations need agreed suppliers.
- **Service duration:** a handover-only booking is different from a team maintaining the spread.
- **Collection arrangements:** later equipment collection and clearance need separate coordination.

For myCHEF catering enquiries, describe the result you want rather than requesting an undefined package. For example, say that you want the table assembled before guests arrive and ask whether maintenance and clearance can be included.

That wording creates a useful discussion without assuming a particular menu, staffing arrangement or inclusion.

## Can a grazing table accommodate dietary requirements?

Dietary requirements belong in the first brief, before the menu and layout are agreed. Give the caterer specific information about allergies, intolerances, vegetarian or vegan preferences and any halal requirements.

Ask which foods can be adapted and which need separate preparation, utensils or serving areas. **An ingredient label does not establish that a shared display is suitable for someone with an allergy.** Confirm the handling arrangements directly with the caterer and the affected guest.

An illustrative layout might separate savoury items, bread, fruit and dips into clearly identified serving areas. This is a planning example, not a myCHEF menu or a guarantee of dietary suitability.

If a guest needs a separately prepared portion, discuss that explicitly. Do not rely on removing an ingredient from the finished table after everything has been arranged.

## Does the catering team stay and replenish the grazing table?

Replenishment is a service responsibility, not an automatic consequence of on-site setup. Ask whether the team leaves after assembly, remains for an agreed period or returns later to collect equipment.

If someone stays, define what “replenishment” means. It might involve bringing out food held back from the agreed menu; it does not, by itself, promise additional food beyond the booking.

Also identify who replaces utensils, tidies the display and answers guests’ dietary questions. The guide to [serving staff and catering cleanup](https://www.mychef.ae/blog/can-catering-companies-in-dubai-provide-serving-staff-and-cleanup) covers the next question to resolve when setup alone is not enough.

## What should you send with your enquiry?

Send a brief that lets the caterer assess the event and ask useful follow-up questions. A clear brief is more valuable than several inspiration photographs with no practical details.

Include:

- The event date and venue location.
- The expected guest count and occasion.
- Whether the grazing table replaces or accompanies a meal.
- The guest arrival time and desired ready time.
- Photographs and measurements of the proposed table.
- Dietary requirements and any separate portions needed.
- Whether you need assembly only, ongoing service or clearance too.

Add your presentation references after these details. Identify what you like about each reference, such as separate serving boards or a compact layout, rather than assuming the entire pictured setup is included.

## FAQ


**Can a caterer assemble a grazing table inside my Dubai home?**

Yes, on-site assembly is a catering format you can request for a home event. Confirm access, the table, food-handling facilities and the setup scope before booking.

**Is grazing table setup the same as platter delivery?**

No. On-site setup means arranging the agreed display at your venue, while platter delivery leaves the final arrangement to you unless setup is specifically included.

**Do I need to provide the table?**

You need to agree who provides the table before booking. Ask separately about furniture, linen, surface protection and serving equipment rather than assuming they come with the food.

**How long does on-site grazing table setup take?**

Ask the caterer for a setup window based on your menu, display and venue access. Agree both an arrival window and a ready time, rather than treating delivery time as the moment guests can start eating.

**Can I put a grazing table outside in Dubai?**

An outdoor grazing table needs a caterer-approved location and food-handling plan. Discuss the conditions, menu suitability and an indoor alternative before confirming the arrangement.

**Will the caterer clean up after the event?**

Cleanup is included only when your agreed scope says so. Specify food removal, waste handling, equipment collection and the surfaces or areas to be cleaned.

**Can I ask myCHEF about grazing table setup for an event?**

Yes, you can send myCHEF an event catering enquiry describing the grazing table you want. Include the date, location, guest count and service required so the setup scope can be discussed without assuming inclusions.


## Before you book, settle the handover

The most useful final question is simple: **who is responsible for the table once the setup team leaves?** Agree that answer alongside the menu. It determines who handles utensils, food left in reserve, guest questions and the end-of-event clear-away.

For a tailored myCHEF catering enquiry, send your date, Dubai location, guest count and service required. State whether you need on-site grazing table assembly only, or assembly with replenishment and clearance, and include photographs of the proposed space.
